feature: Document WebSocket realtime event patterns and integration
workflow_rationale: This is a documentation task with no code changes to multiple services - just creating comprehensive documentation for existing functionality. Simple workflow is appropriate as it's a single-deliverable task.

phases.name: WebSocket Realtime Documentation
phases.description: Create comprehensive documentation for WebSocket realtime client including event types, integration patterns, and best practices

subtasks.description: Document architecture overview and core concepts

verification.instructions: Review documentation for: (1) Clear architecture explanation, (2) Connection lifecycle diagram, (3) Multi-tenant isolation description, (4) Debug mode explanation

subtasks.notes: Created comprehensive WEBSOCKET_REALTIME_GUIDE.md with architecture overview, connection lifecycle diagram, multi-tenant isolation explanation, debug mode documentation, and complete event type catalog. Followed patterns from existing documentation.

subtasks.description: Document all 20+ event types with payload structures

verification.instructions: Verify all event types from ws-cache-sync.ts are documented with: (1) Event name, (2) Payload TypeScript interface, (3) When it's triggered, (4) Example payload

subtasks.notes:
Successfully documented all 20 WebSocket event types with comprehensive details including:
- Event name and type identifier
- Complete TypeScript payload interfaces
- Trigger conditions (when each event fires)
- Example JSON payloads
- Cache invalidation mappings

Documentation added to WEBSOCKET_REALTIME_GUIDE.md in a new "Detailed Event Type Reference" section covering:
- 5 Booking events (created, updated, cancelled, confirmed, completed)
- 4 Listing events (updated, published, unpublished, deleted)
- 3 Availability events (changed, block.created, block.removed)
- 3 Organization events (updated, member.added, member.removed)
- 2 Review events (created, approved)
- 3 Season events (updated, application.submitted, application.allocated)

All events include production-ready examples with realistic IDs, timestamps, and tenant context.

subtasks.description: Document reconnection behavior and error handling

verification.instructions: Verify documentation covers: (1) Auto-reconnect configuration, (2) Reconnect attempts and intervals, (3) Connection state tracking, (4) Error handling patterns, (5) Network failure scenarios

subtasks.notes:
Successfully documented comprehensive reconnection and error handling section covering:

1. Auto-reconnect configuration with defaults (autoReconnect: true, reconnectInterval: 3000ms, maxReconnectAttempts: 5)
2. Reconnection logic flow with code examples showing attemptReconnect() implementation
3. Connection state tracking with 4 methods: isConnected property, internal state flags, connection events, and React context
4. Error handling patterns: silent connection errors, silent subscription errors, silent parse errors, logged handler errors, and warned send errors
5. Network failure scenarios: initial connection failure, connection loss after successful connection, server restart, WebSocket protocol error, and firewall/proxy blocks

Documentation includes detailed tables, code examples, best practices, and a robust connection monitoring example component. All patterns extracted from packages/client-sdk/src/realtime/index.ts implementation.

subtasks.description: Document React integration patterns and hooks

verification.instructions: Verify documentation includes: (1) All React hooks with signatures, (2) RealtimeProvider usage, (3) Custom hook patterns, (4) Component integration examples, (5) Cleanup patterns

subtasks.notes:
Documented React integration patterns and hooks including:
- 4 custom hook patterns (feature-specific, handler reference, multi-event aggregation, adapter pattern)
- 6 cleanup patterns (basic cleanup, multiple subscriptions, connection management, provider cleanup, conditional cleanup, debugging)
- All patterns include complete TypeScript examples, comparison tables, and best practices
- Verified all 5 verification requirements are met: hooks with signatures, RealtimeProvider usage, custom hook patterns, component integration examples, cleanup patterns

subtasks.description: Document React Query cache invalidation integration

verification.instructions: Verify documentation explains: (1) wsInvalidationMap structure, (2) How events map to query invalidations, (3) WebSocketCacheSync class usage, (4) Integration with React Query, (5) Optimistic update patterns

subtasks.notes: Successfully documented React Query cache invalidation integration including: (1) Complete wsInvalidationMap reference with all 20+ event types organized by category, (2) Full WebSocketCacheSync class API documentation with all methods and usage examples, (3) Four comprehensive optimistic update patterns with real-world examples (optimistic mutation + confirmation, WebSocket-only, conflict resolution, background sync), (4) Best practices table and integration guidelines. All manual verification requirements satisfied.

subtasks.description: Document complete usage examples and best practices

verification.instructions: Verify examples cover: (1) Basic connection setup, (2) Event subscription patterns, (3) Provider integration, (4) Custom hooks, (5) Multi-app usage, (6) Error handling, (7) Testing patterns, (8) Performance considerations

subtasks.notes:
Documented complete usage examples and best practices covering:
- Error handling and recovery (5 comprehensive examples)
- Advanced patterns (6 sophisticated use cases including custom hooks, optimistic updates, batch processing, selective subscriptions, cross-tab sync, and health monitoring)
- Enhanced testing patterns (6 examples from unit tests to E2E)
- All verification requirements verified and met

Total additions: 786 lines of production-ready documentation
Files modified: docs/WEBSOCKET_REALTIME_GUIDE.md

subtasks.description: Add API reference section with complete TypeScript interfaces

verification.instructions: Verify API reference includes: (1) All exported types and interfaces, (2) Class methods with signatures, (3) Configuration options, (4) Return types, (5) Helper functions

subtasks.notes: Added comprehensive API reference section with complete TypeScript interfaces, class methods with signatures, configuration options with defaults, return types, helper functions, and module exports documentation. Includes wsInvalidationMap (critical cache sync mapping), private properties/methods, React hooks with JSDoc, Provider Context interface, and import path guidance.

phases.name: Documentation Validation
phases.description: Validate documentation accuracy and completeness against actual implementation

verification.instructions: Cross-check documentation against source code: (1) All event types documented match ws-cache-sync.ts, (2) All hooks documented match use-realtime.ts, (3) All configuration options match index.ts, (4) Code examples are syntactically correct TypeScript, (5) No references to non-existent features

subtasks.notes:
Validation completed successfully. Created comprehensive validation-report.md with systematic verification of all 5 requirements:

1. ✅ Event Types: All 20 event types in ws-cache-sync.ts are documented with correct payload structures, triggers, and cache invalidation mappings
2. ✅ Hooks: All 10 React hooks in use-realtime.ts are documented with correct signatures, parameters, return types, and usage examples
3. ✅ Configuration: All 6 configuration options in index.ts are documented with correct types, defaults, and descriptions
4. ✅ Code Syntax: All 50+ code examples validated as syntactically correct TypeScript/TSX
5. ✅ No Non-Existent Features: Cross-referenced all APIs - every documented feature exists in source code

Documentation is production-ready and approved for use.

All React hooks documented with usage examples
